section_4b_pre_print_debates.title: 1. Blackwell GB200 Architecture Deployment Pace & Liquid Cooling Scaling
section_4b_pre_print_debates.content: CoreWeave was the first cloud provider to receive production Nvidia Blackwell B200 and GB200 NVL72 clusters. Analysts will aggressively interrogate CEO Michael Intrator on liquid cooling manifold readiness, facility power density (120 kW/rack), and whether Nvidia allocations remain unconstrained amid global packaging capacity tightness.

section_4b_pre_print_debates.title: 2. High Debt Service, CapEx Intensity & Forensic True FCF Conversion (-$5,908M)
section_4b_pre_print_debates.content: In Q2 2026, CoreWeave generated $679M in Operating Cash Flow but spent $6,422M in CapEx, resulting in True FCF of -$5,908M (including $165M SBC). With total enterprise value of $70.15B vs market cap of $25.55B, net debt exceeds $44B. Institutional desks demand clarity on debt refinancing schedules, equipment financing interest rates, and payback horizons per GPU cluster.

section_4b_pre_print_debates.title: 3. Short Interest Crowding (22.4% Float) & Hyperscaler Customer Concentration
section_4b_pre_print_debates.content: With short float at 22.4% and an options-implied earnings move of ±22.88%, CoreWeave presents massive pre-print asymmetry. Bears highlight that over 65% of revenue originates from two frontier AI foundation labs. A diversified Q3 customer backlog addition or sovereign AI deal announcement would spark an immediate short squeeze toward mean PT ($132.18, +185% upside).
